questions.q: A reporter says, 'I didn't shape it; I just found the story in the facts.' What would Hayden White reply?
choices: The facts limit what you can say, but you chose the kind of story they became
Stories should begin with a nut graf
The story lies in the reporter's personal insight
questions.explain: Emplotment is a choice the evidence doesn't dictate.

questions.q: Which set are White's four modes of emplotment?
questions.explain: He borrowed them from Northrop Frye's Anatomy of Criticism (1957).

questions.q: Where do White's four plot types originally come from?
questions.explain: The types are Frye's; applying them to history-writing is White's move.

questions.q: Why, according to 'The Value of Narrativity', do we prefer narrative history to annals?
choices: Narrative closure gives events a moral meaning
questions.explain: Ending a story is a way of judging it; narrative is bound up with the urge to moralize.

questions.q: How does 'We tell ourselves stories in order to live' function in Didion's essay?
choices: As the thesis of a celebration of storytelling
As a prelude to doubt about the stories she'd told herself
As a quote from one of the Manson trial witnesses
questions.explain: The essay goes on to show events refusing to cohere into narrative.

questions.q: A reporter covering a chaotic week of events finds no arc fits. What does Didion's 'The White Album' model?
choices: Force the events into a hero's journey
A fragmented structure that admits the material resists narrative
Lead with the most important fact
questions.explain: Didion's form, fragments and lists, is part of her argument.

questions.q: What criticism was raised against White at the 1990 conference published as Probing the Limits of Representation?
choices: That some events, like the Holocaust, may not rightly be told in just any mode
That he relied too heavily on Freud
That his modes were too numerous
questions.explain: Scholars pressed him on whether choice of plot is limited by the events themselves.

ideas: Historians don't find plots in the past; they give events the shape of romance, tragedy, comedy or satire.
Medieval annals that list hard winters and blank years show what records look like without narrative closure.
Narrative closure is a way of moralizing reality: to end a story is to judge it.
We tell ourselves stories in order to live, and some years those stories stop working.
